# SkillPot

SkillPot is a library of practical, selectively installable agent instructions. It is not an agent runtime, registry, or installer. Published collection v0.4.1 remains pinned at ten skills; current source has twelve bundles, including original claim-check and change-impact 0.1.0, unreleased and not in v0.4.1. Upstream product projects remain canonical.

## Start
Published v0.4.1 contains ten skills: seven pinned public project/contributor packages covering Intpot, Summonpot, Dexpot and Refpot, plus the original repository-readiness, decision-brief and document-actions workflows. Current source retains those ten and adds claim-check and change-impact, two unreleased working artifacts; this is not a change to the published snapshot. Install only claim-check with `npx skills@1.7.6 add https://github.com/tugrulguner/skillpot/tree/4139aff1dd8127fc4c9bb3916a4bc5e3fd5cd23c --skill claim-check` (Node.js 22.20.0+ and Git required). See the [claim-check first-use guide](https://github.com/tugrulguner/skillpot/blob/main/docs/claim-check-first-use.md). Change-impact maps a specified code change to evidence-backed consequences in impact.md and focused check recommendations in verification.md, without modifying code or running tests by default. Static dependency evidence is not runtime reachability. See its [one-command first-use guide](https://github.com/tugrulguner/skillpot/blob/main/docs/change-impact-first-use.md). This discovery establishes availability, not task efficacy. Document-actions extracts source-stated assignments and requirements into actions.md and questions.md, keeping proposals and completed/cancelled history separate, deadlines verbatim and conflicts explicit. It does not invent acceptance or operate a task tracker. Decision-brief produces a proposed recommendation and evidence ledger from a bounded input packet; it does not accept or implement the decision. Use the stable v0.4.1 checkout for any selected released workflow; first-use steps pin release commit 79284b3faa928dc556a9032aa9dbeb059b4ee915. Refpot is a preview and repository-readiness remains experimental. Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and Hermes use their documented native skill mechanisms. Installation copies instructions, not product dependencies or additional authority. Full MIT source notices are retained per package.
